title: Anime short hair: shared-root shell plus modular clumps
summary: Candidate authoring method for stylized mesh hair: keep shared-root continuity where it matters, use independent ribbon clumps where local deformation matters, and preserve special curls/forks as reusable accent sources instead of forcing one universal generator.
terms: anime short hair bangs shared root shell ribbon clump mesh hair
stylized character hair topology layered clumps fringe side back

uses: choosing between connected shell patches and independent clumps
small head-only hair experiments before full-character adoption

principle.invariant: Choose topology by the relationship the region must preserve, not by a single universal hair primitive.
families: SHARED_ROOT_SHELL: scalp-conformed local patch, longitudinal flow, partial slits, preserved root bridge, independently shaped strip tips
SOLID_RIBBON_CLUMP: thin prism/ribbon/wedge with control sections for bend, width, depth, roll, taper and tip
COMPOUND_ACCENT_CLUMP: authored or modular curl/fork/hook/hane source kept when a generic generator would lose silhouette quality
principle.layering: Topology family and hairstyle role are separate. BASE/PRIMARY/INNER/ACCENT describe visual function, not construction.
principle.selection: Continuity-heavy region -> consider shell; independently deforming lock -> consider ribbon clump; identity-heavy special curl/fork -> consider compound/manual source.
principle.reference_fit: Prioritize front/side silhouette, bangs-to-face boundary, negative space around face, parting/flow, then depth and accents.

procedure.shared_root_shell: surface fit -> control sections -> longitudinal flow topology -> partial slit/cut graph -> preserve root bridge -> strip-tip shaping
procedure.solid_ribbon_clump: ribbon/prism/wedge -> section placement -> bend/roll -> width/depth -> taper -> tip shaping
procedure.assembly: combine families as needed -> layer primary/inner/accent -> tune overlap and silhouette -> keep source editable -> derive consumer output only when needed

experiment.pattern: Preserve the accepted source, use a duplicate candidate .blend or isolated collection, derive/copy only the head/scalp needed, test representative hair approaches, inspect front/side/3-4 and close topology, and request human visual audit when it would resolve a genuine ambiguity.
examples: shared-root front shell vs fully independent front clumps
manual ribbon clumps vs curve-driven wrappers
manual accent source vs generalized generator

evidence.basis: User-provided chronological summary and still frames inspected 2026-09-15; practitioner source https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QjwhdX6AHnU
evidence.claim: Frames show a local scalp-conformed patch with longitudinal/cross-loop topology and partial slits, plus independent ribbon/wedge clumps, compound curled elements and layered exploded assembly. The three-family abstraction is an inferred reusable interpretation.

limits: Not host-replayed from the full source video in this repo.

promotion.next: Use only when relevant; if a real character/head-only test succeeds and the method saves work, add the tested result and limits. Revise or retire it if the transfer fails.
